title: Tenant-centric log mapper and OpenTelemetry hook adapter for multi-tenant Loki pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a tenant-aware log mapping layer + OpenTelemetry (OTel) server-side hook adapter that normalizes structured logs, preserves correlation IDs, and routes enriched events into the Loki-based aggregation pipeline with predictable resource usage.

Background: Our multi-tenant ingest is increasingly brittle: tenant identifiers are scattered across different fields, some services emit mixed JSON/plaintext, and correlation IDs are inconsistently propagated. Downstream dashboards (latency/error) rely on a canonical tenant ID and a stable correlation id (trace/span linkage). Existing work (ENG-41208, ENG-52317) addressed parts of enrichment and schema adapters but left a gap for a lightweight inline mapper that runs before heavy transformations.

Scope:
- Implement an OTel-compatible hook adapter that can be deployed at the ingress edge (ingest-proxy) and invoked by the OTel collector pipeline.
- Provide a tenant mapping policy engine that: 1) extracts tenant ID via a configurable priority list (headers -> body.json.tenant -> metadata mappings), 2) normalizes correlation IDs to a canonical key (correlation_id), and 3) emits structured JSON with a validated schema version tag.
- Integrate with existing Loki labels/tenant routing so tenant-aware sharding and retention policies are applied.
- Add lightweight normalization rules (no full regex engines in the hot path) and fallbacks to async workers for expensive operations.

Design notes:
- The mapper runs in two modes: inline (fast path) and fallback (async enrichment). Inline must complete in < 2ms P95 per event.
- Use compiled, pre-validated JSONPath and header matchers to avoid runtime regex costs.
- Correlation ID canonicalization: accept hyphenated UUIDs, 64-bit hex, and plaintext tokens; store both raw and canonical forms for trace reconstitution.
- Emit logs with schema_version and source_hints labels so downstream consumers can apply the right parser (see Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tenant+Log+Mapper).

Rollout plan:
1) Spike and unit tests in a feature branch; validate extraction heuristics using 10k anonymized sample events from prod-sample (sanitized).
2) Deploy to staging with feature-flagged inference and run dashboards to compare ingest latency and error surface (Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/ingest-latency).
3) Canary to 5% of tenants with circuit-breaker and quick rollback path.
4) Full ramp if error rate and latency within SLOs.

Success criteria (must pass before full ramp):
- P95 ingest latency increase <= 4ms compared to baseline (without mapper).
- Correlation ID coverage improves from 68% to >=95% on sampled traces.
- No increase in downstream log parsing errors > 0.5% above baseline.
- Observability dashboards show stable CPU/memory in the ingest-proxy (no unbounded memory growth).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Inline normalization could increase CPU. Mitigation: compiled matchers + offload heavy transforms to async pipeline (ENG-251009 will track the async worker optimization).
- Risk: Schema drift breaks downstream parsers. Mitigation: include schema_version and add consumers to fall back gracefully; maintain compatibility tests that run against downstream parsers.
- Risk: Tenant spoofing via header injection. Mitigation: prefer signed metadata (where available) and fall back to tenant lists; require security review (see security_review_required).

Testing:
- Unit tests for all matcher permutations and canonicalization rules.
- Integration tests with OTel collector config variations.
- Load test with 100k events/sec in staging to validate resource cost and tail latency.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tenant+Log+Mapper
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10234
- Test dataset: gs://redwood-prod-samples/observability/tenant-mapper-sanitized-2026-01

Notes: This ticket focuses on the ingress mapping and OTel adapter. Downstream enrichment and long-running normalization tasks should be split into follow-ups and tracked separately (see ENG-251009, ENG-261100).
